summary: Iteration 10 — TTL index on db.location_shares.expires_at + profile activity status (last_active_human / is_online). Backend: 17/17 pytest pass: TTL index 'ttl_expires_at' exists with expireAfterSeconds=0 on expires_at; POST /api/safety/share-location stores BSON datetime (not ISO string); GET location/{match_id} returns sharing=false+expired=true when expiry is in the past; legacy ISO-string fallback works without crashing; /api/profile/{id}, /api/discover, /api/matches all surface last_active_human + is_online; last_active throttle (60s window) verified — 5 rapid /api/auth/me calls do NOT move db.users.last_active; all 7 human_last_active edge cases (Active now, Xm, Xh, yesterday, Xd, Xw, Xmo) verified by manipulating DB timestamps; is_online true<5min / false>=5min. Frontend smoke (mobile 390x844, demo1 login): /discover shows data-testid='activity-status' + 'activity-dot' + 'activity-text' ('Active 3h ago') on profile card; /matches shows green online-dot with data-testid='online-dot-0a019632-6f9f-45ab-8fb6-20601b4e60f3' on demo2's avatar (demo2 was recently active from the iter9 message hook test). No console errors.

minor.issue: Boundary at exactly 7 days uses days<7 → so day 6 = '6d ago', day 7 = '1w ago'. Same for 30 (days<30) and < 3600. Boundaries documented and consistent.

last_active bump uses asyncio.create_task without awaiting — fire-and-forget. If the create_task is cancelled (e.g. server shutdown mid-request), the bump silently drops. Acceptable for a non-critical throttled counter, but worth a docstring note.

When expires_at is naive datetime (very old BSON without tz), code does `expires.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` — implicit assumption that all stored datetimes are UTC. OK because POST writes datetime.now(timezone.utc), but worth a comment.
duration_minutes is clamped 15-240 silently — passing 5 becomes 15, passing 999 becomes 240. No validation error returned. Consider 422 on out-of-range or document the clamp behaviour in OpenAPI.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 3618 lines — same urgency as iter9. Router split is overdue (routers/safety.py, routers/profile.py, services/presence.py for human_last_active/is_online).
human_last_active() and is_online_now() are pure helpers — perfect candidates for /app/backend/services/presence.py. Currently buried mid-file at line 2212.
last_active throttle window (60s) is hardcoded — could be a module constant LAST_ACTIVE_THROTTLE_SECONDS = 60 for tunability.
is_online 5-minute window is also hardcoded inside is_online_now() — extract to ONLINE_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300 for product team to tune without code dive.

Legacy ISO-string fallback in get_shared_location adds branching every call — once the production DB is fully migrated to BSON datetime (which the startup purge does on cold-start), the fallback becomes dead code. Add a TODO with a removal date.

The TTL index purge on startup uses to_list(500) — if a deployment has >500 legacy ISO docs, only the first batch is purged. Make it a while-loop or paginate. (For this scale, 500 is plenty, but worth fixing.)

The 'profile.last_active_human' field is computed per-request for every profile in /api/discover — inexpensive (string format from a single ISO), but if the discover feed grows to 50+ profiles per page, consider a precomputed `last_active_bucket` field updated by a cron. For now, OK.

is_online is computed at read time — means a profile that goes online won't update on currently-rendered Discover/Matches lists without a re-fetch. Frontend should poll/refresh on focus, or WS event when a peer's last_active crosses the 5-min threshold. Not in scope for this iter but worth noting.
No index on db.users.last_active — if you ever query 'who's online right now' (e.g. for nudge campaigns), add an index. Currently unused as a filter so not a perf issue.
